q: Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path. Do not trade circular path for straight line or parabolic path.

q: In circular motion, even if speed is constant, velocity is not constant because _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. In circular motion, even if speed is constant, velocity is not constant because direction changes continuously. Do not trade direction changes continuously for speed changes or mass changes.

q: The velocity in circular motion is also called _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. The velocity in circular motion is also called tangential velocity. Do not trade tangential velocity for radial velocity or angular velocity.

q: Angular displacement $\theta$ is defined as the ratio of _____ to radius.
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Angular displacement θ is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius. Chord length or diameter is not this quantity.

q: The SI unit of angular displacement is the _____ .
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. The SI unit of angular displacement is the radian. Do not trade radian for degree or revolution.

q: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the _____ .
e: One radian is the angle at the centre when the arc length equals the radius. One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius. Diameter or circumference is not this quantity.

q: The relation $1 \text{ rev} = 2\pi \text{ rad}$ implies that $360^{\circ}$ equals _____ .
e: The relation 1 rev = 2π rad implies that 360° equals 2π rad. π rad or (π)/(2) rad is a different relation from 2π rad.

q: Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to _____ .
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to time taken. Do not trade time taken for distance traveled or radius.

q: Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the _____ of angular displacement.
a: first derivative with respect to time
second derivative with respect to time
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the first derivative with respect to time of angular displacement. Do not trade first derivative with respect to time for second derivative with respect to time or integral over time.

q: The unit of angular velocity is NOT _____ .
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The unit of angular velocity is NOT m s^-1. Rad s^-1 or rpm is not this quantity.

q: Average angular acceleration is the ratio of the change in angular velocity to _____ .
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Average angular acceleration is the ratio of the change in angular velocity to time taken. Do not trade time taken for angular displacement or radius.

q: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of _____ .
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Angular displacement or linear velocity is not this quantity.

q: The relation between tangential speed $v$ and angular speed $\omega$ is _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. The relation between tangential speed v and angular speed ω is v = ω r. v = ω / r or v = ω² r is a different relation from v = ω r.

q: The relation between tangential acceleration $a_t$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$ is _____ .
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. The relation between tangential acceleration a_t and angular acceleration α is a_t = α r. a_t = α / r or a_t = α² r is a different relation from a_t = α r.

q: In uniform circular motion, the angular acceleration is _____ .
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. In uniform circular motion, the angular acceleration is zero. Constant and non-zero or increasing is not this quantity.

q: Angular velocity and angular acceleration are _____ quantities.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Angular velocity and angular acceleration are vector quantities. Scalar or dimensionless is not this quantity.

q: The direction of linear (tangential) acceleration in circular motion is _____ to the path.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. The direction of linear (tangential) acceleration in circular motion is tangential to the path. Radial or perpendicular is not this quantity.

q: If a disc rotates at 45 rpm, its angular speed in rad s$^{-1}$ is _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. If a disc rotates at 45 rpm, its angular speed in rad s^-1 is 1.5π. (π)/(2) or 3π is a different relation from 1.5π.

q: A particle rotating with uniform angular speed undergoes _____ .
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. A particle rotating with uniform angular speed undergoes uniform circular motion. Non-uniform circular motion or linear motion is not this quantity.

q: Which of the following is NOT a unit of angular acceleration?
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Which of the following is NOT a unit of angular acceleration? Do not trade m s^-2 for rad s^-2 or rev s^-2.
